corrections.caveats: Enricher: the signed int counters i_ (after about 2,000 iterations) and i (at Google Benchmark's iteration counts) overflow in every row, undefined behaviour though timing is likely unaffected; the verifier's loop-folding and devirtualisation notes are confirmed. Base and derived share the name f, so a derived class without f recurses forever (the repo's own 02_bad_crtp.C; 03_good_crtp.C fixes it with f_impl). No build files in Chapter08; last code upload 2023-06-19.

Enricher: bugs confirmed from source and by a reduced build: ScopeGuardTypeErasedFast redeclares mutable bool commit_, shadowing the base flag, so commit() never disarms the guard and a moved-from guard still runs the cleanup (twice in total). The alignas(8) buffer has no alignof static_assert, so an over-aligned capture is undefined behaviour; an lvalue callable fails the static_assert; the file relies on transitive includes. rand() plus new/delete dominate the timed loop; the gain is only 0.7-0.8 ns.

Enricher: each wrapper is built in the same function as its timed loop, so the compiler sees the stored target and the amount of devirtualisation depends on the compiler; the gap is under 0.5 ns per call. libstdc++ std::function also stores trivially copyable callables up to 16 bytes inline, so neither side allocates; the gain is in the call path (no empty check per call, arguments by value rather than _ArgTypes&&). Fits smart-pointers-and-refcount poorly.

Enricher: the harness is sound (allocation in a separate file, the destroy call stays indirect), but the baseline is lopsided: shared_ptr pays for a control block and reference counting, and the book's variants do not beat unique_ptr. Sibling classes smartptr_te_lb and smartptr_te_lb0 compare sizeof(Deleter) with the buffer instead of sizeof(destroy<Deleter>), which adds a vtable pointer, so a 9-16 byte deleter overflows the buffer (the benchmark's empty deleter hides it). No copy or move operations, so any copy double-deletes.

Enricher: off-by-one bugs confirmed by running a reduced copy (GCC 13.3): pushing 100..106 reads back 0, 100..105, and 17 of 20 pushes are accepted (issue #22, open since 2024-04-27, no reply); the timed work is the same push/pop loop, so the speed comparison stands but the container is not correct. SetItemsProcessed is 7x low on both sides (ratio unaffected). No build files; the unmerged CMake PR #8 sets no build type or flags. etl::queue<T, SIZE> is a correct fixed-capacity alternative.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Book (relayed via the seed lead from the book, not shown on any repo page I opened): in the null-pointer (nodelete) rows the template guard matches explicit code while the std::function guard costs about 1.7-1.8 ns more, about 1.4x (derived from the relayed numbers). The delete rows (template 4.56 ns, explicit 4.54 ns, std::function 13.4 ns, about 2.9x) are not valid evidence: the compiler elides new/delete in the explicit and template rows but not in the std::function row.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: assembly of a reduced copy (GCC 13.3, Clang 18, -O2/-O3) shows the explicit and template delete rows drop new/delete entirely while the std::function and buffer-guard rows keep operator new, so the 2.9x delete-row figure compares elided allocation with real allocation and is not valid; the guard's real overhead is the nodelete row, about 1.7-1.8 ns (about 1.4x). MakeGuard on an lvalue lambda does not compile (both constructors collapse to one signature), and with only <functional> GCC 13 rejects std::exchange (the file never includes <utility>).

Enricher: asymmetric harness: only the cast row uses DoNotOptimize, so the virtual row's result is never observed and the compiler can devirtualise and fold the 64 calls; the virtual row is a --i chain through heap memory while the cast row is a side-effect-free type test, so the rows do different work. The repo never says whether the book's 1 ns versus 5-10 ns is per operation or per 64-operation iteration. No build files; the .C extension needs /TP on MSVC.

Enricher: hardware_concurrency() can return 0 (division by zero); every worker calls std::forward<F>(f) on the same functor, so a stateful rvalue functor is moved from concurrently (data race); a worker throw or a std::thread constructor throw ends in std::terminate. One run per size with the sequential version always first; results feed only assert, so an NDEBUG build can eliminate the sequential work (bias against the parallel version). CMake gives GCC/Clang only -g; the README's VS2022 line uses -A Win32 (32-bit); the top-level add_subdirectory(chapterNN) does not match the ChapterNN folders, so configure fails on Linux (issue #7, open, no reply).

Enricher: fold seeds each chunk with R{}, so product, min and max give wrong results, and version2 combines halves with a hard-coded + instead of op; the rvalue functor is std::forward-ed once per task (use-after-move for stateful functors); hardware_concurrency() == 0 divides by zero. Top-level CMake configure fails on Linux (issue #7); main.cpp runs all Chapter 8 recipes in one process and checks results only by assert. The fold baseline is 58689 us here against 41374 us in the std::thread recipe (about 42% slower), suggesting the 4.5x is inflated.

Enricher: most of the gap is the idiom (no reserve plus std::vector::at bounds checks); std::vector<int>(n) zero-fills, so use reserve or make_unique_for_overwrite to match new[]. Qt 6 QList::at() is noexcept and checks bounds only through Q_ASSERT_X (qtbase 6.5 qlist.h), so QVector being slowest fits a Debug build (inference). Vector growth peaks near 0.8 GB (derived). The signed int sum overflows (undefined behaviour) and unused results let the optimiser elide the array test.

Enricher: confirmed: 01_sharing_incr_mbm.C runs REPEAT64 but reports 32 items, so its atomic items/s is off by 2x (01a is clean). 01a, 01b, 01c, 01e and the mbm file read state.thread_index as a data member, which Google Benchmark v1.6.0 (PR #1208, 2021-08-23) made private behind thread_index(), so they do not compile against current Google Benchmark without edits (only 01d uses thread_index()). No build files; the thread sweep runs to _SC_NPROCESSORS_CONF unpinned, including SMT siblings; POSIX-only despite the README listing MSVC.

Enricher: the harness is symmetric (1024 DoNotOptimize increments plus one shared atomic add on both sides; the benchmark's memory clobber forces each store). 04_local_incr.C and 02_sharing_incr.C use the pre-1.6 Google Benchmark state.thread_index member and do not compile against current releases without edits. The shared accumulators x2 and x3 are unpadded globals next to the arrays. folly pads to 128 bytes (adjacent-line prefetch since Sandy Bridge); GCC warns about std::hardware_destructive_interference_size ABI stability (-Winterference-size).

Enricher: matrixMulKernel equals matrixMulKernel_shared except for explicit fmaf, and nvcc fuses to FMA by default while the unroll bound is the runtime blockDim.x, so the whole gain is tiling. checkResults uses an absolute 1e-4 tolerance on outputs near 500 (about 3 ulp); a float32 simulation (host non-FMA versus GPU FMA, same order) has about 1,600 of 4,000,000 outputs differing by 1.22e-4, so the program probably prints 'Results do not match!' for every GPU variant. Shared tiles are fixed at TILE=16 while the loops use blockDim, so only a 16x16 launch is safe; the _row/_col kernels index B with the macro N rather than width. The README build has no build type and the CMake 3.16 dev container sets no CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES.

Enricher: the CPU loop is built with no -O flag (CMakeLists has no flags or build type; whether nvcc optimises host code by default could not be confirmed), so the 44.04x kernel-only figure may rest on an unoptimised baseline (-O0 precedent; D candidate if confirmed). It corresponds to about 242 GB/s on the GPU against about 5.5 GB/s on the CPU (derived); copies from pageable memory run at about 5.8 GB/s, hence 1.02x end to end. No CUDA error checks and h_C is overwritten unchecked, so a failed launch would still print a speedup; one run, no warm-up. Dev container: CUDA 12.0, g++ 9, Ubuntu 20.04.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Chapter02/ReadMe.md (linked from the root README as the how-to-run page) gives the generic build line: $CXX (GCC or Clang) -g -O3 --std=c++17 -lpthread -latomic. Compiler version and CPU of the book's run are not stated.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: only Arg 1<<10 is run and every thread replays the same rand sequence; glibc serves sizes up to 1032 bytes from the per-thread tcache with no lock, so the run measures only the allocator's fast path and the book's 8-thread penalty cannot be checked. The never-taken cout << buf branch is a deliberate escape against dead-code elimination (it would print an unterminated buffer if taken); Buffer::resize copies the old contents for nothing. The CPU is still unstated.

Enricher: the 03b baseline's get() returns .get() of a temporary shared_ptr, so it pays the lock plus a count increment and decrement on every dereference yet protects nothing; all threads contend on one pool mutex (libstdc++ uses 16, libc++ 32); each 03b assign also copies q by value. The commented-out delete cannot be enabled (BM_ptr_assign republishes the same q and would free it) and the initial A(42) leaks. The baseline's atomic_load/atomic_store overloads for shared_ptr are deprecated in C++20, and libstdc++'s C++20 atomic<shared_ptr> uses a control-block lock bit instead, so the 60x is library-specific.
